title: The agent
intro.1: Each session runs the Cua Driver as its agent: it reads the page through its accessibility tree and its screen, and acts through the compositor’s virtual input.
how-you-reach-it.title: How you reach it
how-you-reach-it.1: The admin speaks MCP to the driver over its standard streams, inside the session, and exposes it as one authenticated HTTP call: POST /api/sessions/{id}/agent with {"tool", "arguments"}. The response is the tool’s MCP result.
how-you-reach-it.2: An agent of your own reaches its sessions with a token instead of your login: see Agents.
how-you-reach-it.3: Every call needs the login cookie, the exact Origin, and the X-CSRF-Token from the login.
how-you-reach-it.4: One call runs at a time per session; up to 4 more wait, each up to 30 seconds, and any more are refused without running: 503 with Retry-After, or isError over MCP.
how-you-reach-it.5: Once a call is sent to the agent, it fails if the agent has not answered within 150 seconds. A run_steps batch gets the longer of 120 seconds and the time its steps may take, plus 30 seconds, and at most 600 seconds.
how-you-reach-it.6: An answer comes back when it is at most 16 MiB as the agent sends it and at most 48 MiB once parsed, as the admin counts it (a long array of small values reaches 48 MiB before 16 MiB), and when reading and parsing it, its escaped strings decoded, take at most 88 MiB together. A larger one fails the call, and the agent starts afresh for the next.
how-you-reach-it.7: After the first takeover in a session, results come back redacted and without screenshots (your own chat keeps them) (see Security). A person who takes control as they open a session (see below) takes it over too.
tools.title: Tools
tools.1: The desktop tools are the Cua Driver’s own. These work in every session:
tools.2: inspect_page {selector, html?, limit?} also works in every session. It reads the elements a CSS selector matches in the active tab, with their tags, attributes and text, and their HTML if asked. It runs in a world the page cannot see, over the browser’s private pipe, changes nothing, and never returns a password field’s value.
tools.windows: close_window {} closes the browser window shown on the screen, as its close button would. While the browser has more than one window open (a page’s popup, a site’s app window), the keyboard tools are refused, since every window shares one process and a key could reach the wrong one: the agent closes the windows it does not need, and closing the last one opens the browser again at the session’s first page.
tools.tabs: A session keeps at most BROWSER_MAX_TABS tabs (8 unless the installation sets it). Once the browser has restored its own, a new tab past them closes as it opens, and the agent’s next tool result says so: it closes a tab it no longer needs, which it chooses, then opens the page again.
tools.crashed: When a tab’s page crashes, the agent’s next tool result says so, and whether the browser reached the session’s memory limit: the tab stays on the browser’s error page, and the agent reloads it or opens another address in it. A page that keeps loading content as it is scrolled, and tabs left open, use that memory up.
tools.3: run_javascript {javascript, pid, window_id} needs the session’s Developer tools option, which you choose as you start or resume it; sessions a token starts never have it. It runs in the page’s own world, so it can read a password field, and the debugging endpoint it uses is something sites may notice. With this option, the agent runs as Chrome’s uid in a container of its own that shares Chrome’s network namespace, so it reaches the endpoint on Chrome’s loopback. Its processes are non-dumpable, so Chrome’s uid cannot read into them. Without it, Chrome listens on no debugging port.
when-a-person-takes.title: When a person takes over
when-a-person-takes.1: A person who opens a session nobody holds control of takes it at once, unless control was left with the agent: the agent started the session, the person gave control back, or the agent is using it (a call on it now, or one that ended or was refused in the last 30 seconds; after the person holding control left, by a reload or a closed tab, any use since then). They also watch while control is changing hands, and when the agent’s last call lost its link to the agent (opening a session never stops the agent). Then they take control with one click.
when-a-person-takes.2: The admin refuses new calls at once and waits up to 5 seconds for the call in flight to end.
when-a-person-takes.3: If it does not end, the agent’s container is killed and proven stopped, and it starts again when control comes back.
when-a-person-takes.4: From then on, only the person’s input reaches the browser until they give back.
